```{=html}
<div class="steps">
  <div class="step"><div class="num">1</div><h3>Pick a job</h3><p>Choose a real Colorado posting from the <a href="jobs.html">Job Board</a> and prep a short pitch.</p></div>
  <div class="step"><div class="num">2</div><h3>Interview for ~7 minutes</h3><p>Your pod of about 4 plays the hiring panel. You answer as yourself.</p></div>
  <div class="step"><div class="num">3</div><h3>Rotate</h3><p>Then you join the panel for everyone else. Each panelist plays a <a href="panel.html">character</a>.</p></div>
```

Nothing to print. Everything is on this site, on your phone or laptop.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Online student?
Same activity on your own schedule. Your pod has two weeks to find one hour together, and there's a video option if you can't. See [Online Students](online.qmd).
:::

## Before class

About 30–45 minutes.

1. **Pick a job** on the [Job Board](jobs.qmd), plus a backup. It's fine if a podmate picks the same one.
2. **Read the real posting** (linked on each job page). Find their top 3 must-haves, and jot down a real example of yours for each.
3. **Practice a 60-second pitch** out loud. Use the toolkit below.
4. **Write one question** you'd genuinely want to ask the panel.
5. **Bring a charged device.**

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
**On your own job's page, stop at "Know the employer."** The Interview room below that is for the panel. Not knowing the questions is part of the practice.
:::

## In class

Each round takes **10 minutes**, and the [Timer](timer.qmd) keeps every pod in step.

| Time | What happens |
|---|---|
| **1 min · Set up** | The candidate names their job. Panelists open **that job's page**, scroll to the **Interview room**, open **their own seat**, and draw a mood card. |
| **1 min · Pitch** | The candidate gives their 60-second pitch. The panel listens. |
| **5 min · Questions** | Each panelist, in seat order, asks one question in character and follows up. |
| **1 min · Your question** | The candidate asks the panel their question. |
| **2 min · Debrief** | Everyone drops character. Each panelist gives three one-line notes (below). |

Then rotate to the next person.

## What's my seat? {#who-sits-where-rotation}

Number off around your pod (1, 2, 3, …). Then pick your pod size and your number:

```{=html}
<div class="seat-picker" id="seat-picker">
  <div><span class="row-label">Pod size</span>
    <div class="btn-group" role="group" aria-label="Pod size" id="sp-size"></div></div>
  <div><span class="row-label">I'm number</span>
    <div class="btn-group" role="group" aria-label="Your number" id="sp-num"></div></div>
  <ol id="sp-out" aria-live="polite"></ol>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  const NAMES = {
    "A": "Seat A · Riley, the Technical Lead",
    "B": "Seat B · Pat, Search Committee Chair",
    "C": "Seat C · Morgan, the Team & Mission Lead",
    "D": "Seat D · Dale, the Outside Stakeholder",
    "A+B": "Seat A+B · Riley-Pat, the Hiring Manager"
  };
  const roles = n => n === 3 ? ["Candidate", "A+B", "C"] : ["Candidate", "A", "B", "C", "D"].slice(0, n);
  let size = 4, me = 1;
  try { size = Number(localStorage.getItem("sp-size")) || 4; me = Number(localStorage.getItem("sp-num")) || 1; } catch (e) {}
  const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);

  function buttons(el, values, current, onPick) {
    el.innerHTML = "";
    values.forEach(v => {
      const b = document.createElement("button");
      b.type = "button";
      b.className = "btn btn-sm " + (v === current ? "btn-primary" : "btn-outline-primary");
      b.textContent = v;
      b.setAttribute("aria-pressed", String(v === current));
      b.addEventListener("click", () => onPick(v));
      el.appendChild(b);
    });
  }

  function render() {
    if (me > size) me = size;
    try { localStorage.setItem("sp-size", size); localStorage.setItem("sp-num", me); } catch (e) {}
    buttons($("sp-size"), [3, 4, 5], size, v => { size = v; render(); });
    buttons($("sp-num"), Array.from({ length: size }, (_, i) => i + 1), me, v => { me = v; render(); });
    const r = roles(size);
    $("sp-out").innerHTML = Array.from({ length: size }, (_, i) => {
      const role = r[((me - (i + 1)) % size + size) % size];
      const cand = role === "Candidate";
      return `<li class="${cand ? "cand" : ""}"><span class="r">Round ${i + 1}</span><span>${cand ? "<b>You're the candidate</b>" : NAMES[role]}</span></li>`;
    }).join("");
  }
  render();
})();
</script>
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}

## Debrief: three one-liners

When the debrief starts, drop character. Each panelist says:

1. **Hired-peer moment:** when they sounded like a colleague you'd want.
2. **Hedge moment:** when they rambled, hedged, or sounded like a seminar.
3. **One thing to try** next time.

Be specific ("When you walked through cleaning the streamflow data, I believed you") rather than general ("Good job!").

## Candidate toolkit

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## 60-second pitch formula
> *"I'm [name], and I [your focus]. Most recently I [one concrete thing you built, analyzed, or managed]. I'm interested in [this role] at [this employer] because [something specific from the posting]. I'd bring [the one or two skills they need most]."*
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## STAR for "Tell me about a time…"
- **Situation:** one or two sentences of context.
- **Task:** what *you* were responsible for.
- **Action:** what *you* did. Spend most of your time here, and say "I," not "we."
- **Result:** what happened (with a number if you have one) and what you learned.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## When you don't know something
> *"I haven't used [X] directly. The closest thing I've done is [Y], where I [specific]. Here's how I'd get up to speed on [X]…"*

This beats bluffing every time.
:::

## Ground rules

- **Tough but fair.** The point is realistic practice, not "winning."
- **No illegal questions,** even in character: nothing about age, family, pregnancy, religion, national origin, or disability.
- **Stumbling is the point.** Better to freeze here than in a real interview.
